history.heading: Settlement and colonisation
paragraphs: Kiribati (pronounced "Kiribas") consists of 33 coral atolls and islands in three groups, the Gilbert, Phoenix and Line Islands, spread over 3.5 million square kilometres of the central Pacific. The Gilbert Islands were settled by Austronesian people over 2,000 years ago.

Britain declared a protectorate over the Gilbert and Ellice Islands in 1892, which became a colony. Phosphate mining on Banaba devastated the island, and its people were relocated to Fiji. During the Second World War, the Battle of Tarawa in 1943 was one of the bloodiest of the Pacific War.

history.heading: Independence
paragraphs: The Ellice Islands separated in 1975 to become Tuvalu, and Kiribati became independent on 12 July 1979. Britain and the United States conducted nuclear tests at Kiritimati (Christmas Island) in the 1950s and 1960s. In 1995 Kiribati moved the International Date Line so the whole country shares the same date, making its Line Islands the first place on Earth to greet each new day.

culture.heading: I-Kiribati traditions
paragraphs: Gilbertese (Kiribati) and English are official languages. Most people are Christian, especially Catholic and Protestant. The maneaba, a large meeting house, is the centre of community life, and traditional dance and navigation skills are valued. Fish, coconut and breadfruit are dietary staples.

politics.heading: Republic
paragraphs: Kiribati is a presidential republic. The president (Beretitenti) is elected by popular vote from candidates nominated by parliament. In 2019 Kiribati switched diplomatic recognition from Taiwan to China.

economy.heading: Ocean economy
paragraphs: Kiribati is one of the least developed countries in the Pacific. Fishing licence fees from foreign fleets, mainly for tuna, are the largest source of government revenue. Copra (dried coconut) and seaweed are exported. A sovereign wealth fund from past phosphate revenues helps finance the budget.
Most of the land is just a few metres above sea level, making Kiribati extremely vulnerable to rising sea levels. The currency is the Australian dollar.
